text: One half of a split permanent is “unlocked” if it has the appropriate unlocked designation. See rule 709.5.

title: Unprepared
text: A permanent that becomes unprepared loses the prepared designation. See rule 722, “Preparation Cards.” See also Prepared.

title: Untap
text: To rotate a permanent back to the upright position from a sideways position. See rule 701.26, “Tap and Untap.”

title: Untap Step
text: Part of the turn. This step is the first step of the beginning phase. See rule 502, “Untap Step.”

title: Untap Symbol
text: The untap symbol {Q} in an activation cost means “Untap this permanent.” See rule 107.6.

title: Untapped
text: A default status a permanent may have. See rule 110.5 and rule 701.26, “Tap and Untap.” See also Tapped.

title: Upkeep Step
text: Part of the turn. This step is the second step of the beginning phase. See rule 503, “Upkeep Step.”

title: Vanguard
text:
1. A casual variant in which each player plays the role of a famous character. See rule 902, “Vanguard.”
2. A card type seen only on nontraditional Magic cards in the Vanguard casual variant. A vanguard card is not a permanent. See rule 313, “Vanguards.”

title: Vanishing
text: A keyword ability that limits how long a permanent remains on the battlefield. See rule 702.63, “Vanishing.”

title: Variant
text: An additional set of rules that determines the style of a multiplayer game. See rule 800.2.

title: Vehicle
text: An artifact subtype. Vehicles can become artifact creatures. See rule 301, “Artifacts,” and rule 702.122, “Crew.”

title: Venture into [Quality]
text: A variant of the venture into the dungeon ability that allows a player to bring a dungeon card with [quality] into the game or move a player’s venture marker. See rule 701.49, “Venture into the Dungeon.”

title: Venture into the Dungeon
text: A keyword action that can bring dungeon cards into the game from outside the game or move a player’s venture marker. See rule 701.49, “Venture into the Dungeon.”

title: Venture Marker
text: A marker used to track which room of a dungeon card a player is currently in. See rule 309, “Dungeons.”

title: Vibranium Token
text: A Vibranium token is a colorless Vibranium artifact token with indestructible and “{T}: Add {C}. This mana can’t be spent to cast a nonartifact spell.” For more information about predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

title: Vigilance
text: A keyword ability that lets a creature attack without tapping. See rule 702.20, “Vigilance.”

title: Visit
text: A keyword ability found on Attraction cards. It provides an effect whenever you roll to visit your attractions and get certain results. See rule 702.159, “Visit.”

title: Vote
text: Some cards instruct players to vote from among given options. See rule 701.38, “Vote.”

title: Walker Token
text: A Walker token is a 2/2 black Zombie creature token named Walker. For more information on predefined tokens, see rule 111.10.

title: Wall
text: A creature type with no particular rules meaning. Older cards with the Wall creature type but without defender had an unwritten ability that precluded them from attacking. Those cards have received errata in the Oracle card reference to have defender. Some older cards that referenced the Wall creature type have also received errata. See Defender.

title: Ward
text: A triggered ability that can counter spells or abilities that target the permanent with ward. See rule 702.21, “Ward.”

title: Warp
text: A keyword ability found on permanent cards that allows them to be cast for an alternative cost. See rule 702.185, “Warp.”

title: Waterbend
text: A keyword action. “Waterbend [cost]” means to pay that cost and, for each {1} in that cost, you may tap an untapped artifact or creature you control rather than pay mana. See rule 701.67, “Waterbend.”

title: Web-slinging
text: A keyword ability that allows spells to be cast for an alternative cost by returning a tapped creature you control to its owner’s hand. See rule 702.188, “Web-slinging.”

title: Win the Game
text: There are several ways to win the game. See rule 104, “Ending the Game,” and rules 810.8 (for additional rules for Two-Headed Giant games) and rule 809.5 (for additional rules for Emperor games).

title: Wither
text: A keyword ability that affects how an object deals damage to a creature. See rule 702.80, “Wither.”

title: Wizardcycling
text: See Typecycling.

title: World
text: A supertype that’s normally relevant on enchantments. See rule 205.4, “Supertypes.” See also World Rule.

title: World Rule
text: A state-based action that causes all permanents with the world supertype except the one that has had the world supertype for the shortest amount of time are put into their owners’ graveyards. See rule 704.5k.

title: Worthy
text: A rules term used to describe a creature that’s legendary, not a Villain, and red and/or white. See rule 700.16.

title: X
text: A placeholder for a number that needs to be determined. See rule 107.3.

title: Y
text: See X.

title: You, Your
text: Words that refer to an object’s controller, its would-be controller (if a player is attempting to cast or activate it), or its owner (if it has no controller). See rule 109.5.

title: Zone
text: A place where objects can be during a game. See section 4, “Zones.”

title: Zone-Change Triggers
text: Trigger events that involve objects changing zones. See rule 603.6.
